Theme

Money, work & business · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

rich adjective

having much money

also wealthy, well off, well-to-do, the rich, rich man, loaded with money, loaded, well supplied, he’s worth a lot of money, loaded (with money), be well off

classical

Plaut. Aul. 184: ubi dīves blandē appellat pauperem
Hor. AP 421: dīves agrīs, dīves positīs in fēnore nummīs, rich in land, rich in money lent at interest
Traupman 157

dīves, dīvitis

adjective, third declension, one ending

rich, wealthy

Comparative dītior, superlative dītissimus. As a noun, a rich man; dīvitēs, the rich.

Other words

  • locuplēs, locuplētis — well-to-do, wealthy; properly, rich in land

    adjective, third declension, one ending · also used · classical · Plaut. Trin. 565: Et ego esse locuplēs, vērum nēquīquam volō; Cic. Rep. 2.16 (Lewis & Short)

    Cicero explains it from land, locus: when wealth lay in cattle and land, men were called pecūniōsī et locuplētēs (Rep. 2.16, Lewis & Short).

  • opulentus, opulenta, opulentum — wealthy, opulent

    also used · classical · Plaut. Trin. 493: aequō mendīcus atque ille opulentissimus; Sall. Jug. 16.5 (Lewis & Short)

  • cōpiōsus, cōpiōsa, cōpiōsum — well supplied, wealthy

    adjective, first and second declension; with the ablative of what one has · also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 2.18: tū agrīs, tū aedificiīs, tū argentō, tū familiā, tū rēbus omnibus ōrnātus et cōpiōsus sīs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 102: loaded with money

Examples

  • nēmō nāscitur dīves; quisquis exit in lūcem jussus est lacte et pannō esse contentus

    No one is born rich: whoever comes out into the light is told to be content with milk and a ragSen. Ep. 20.13

  • Nōn temerārium est, ubi dīves blandē appellat pauperem. jam illic homō aurum scit mē habēre, eō mē salūtat blandius.

    It’s no accident when a rich man speaks sweetly to a poor one: he must know I have gold, that’s why he greets me so sweetly.Plaut. Aul. 184–185

  • Dīvitiās maximās habet.

    He’s worth a lot of money.Traupman 112

  • locuplēs esse

    to be well offTraupman 353

See also poor, poverty, resources, property, money.
